To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
passive attention techniques applied to ANNs predict human visual selectivity and that human visual selectivity can predict the performance of ANNs.

(a) passive attention techniques reveal that ANNs have a shared component in their visual selectivity with human observers, (b) the shared component is most pronounced for relatively simple ANN architectures that use guided backpropagation techniques, and (c) this shared component is predictive of recognition performance in both humans and the ANNs.
1) passive attention maps derived from ANNs are a good proxy for human visual selectivity, and 2) the reverse is not true: human visual selectivity is not a good proxy for ANN attention maps.

the extent to which ANNs can serve as models for human vision.
the development of methods that can help us understand and evaluate the biological and psychological plausibility of ANNs.
understanding how ANNs represent the visual world and how these representations are similar to or different from human visual representations.
